title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary; the harmful-change mapping and all per-episode traces required to compute it are archived (see Methods). We report the primary, preregistered confirmatory estimand exactly as archived and provide the precise artifact locations needed to reproduce preregistered secondary safety aggregations.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to assist network operations (NetOps) with intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A standard safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): generate a candidate configuration, check it with a deterministic verifier, and—if violations appear—expose verifier diagnostics to a repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical evidence in program repair and Infrastructure-as-Code shows that interposing deterministic verifiers and exposing diagnostics to repair models can increase verifier-detected pass rates while introducing new failure modes and interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Survey and field studies in NetOps/AIOps caution that read-oriented usefulness of LLMs does not automatically imply safe closed-loop changes [5].

Research question and contribution. Controlled evidence on verifier-guided repair for vendor CLIs using preregistered realistic fault operators is limited. Our research question is: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? We answer this with a preregistered, paired, controlled-fault experiment (planned n=40 pairs) executed under adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared controlled-fault candidates. Primary contribution: an artifact-grounded confirmatory estimate (paired difference, discordant counts, exact paired test and bootstrap CI) showing a substantial improvement for guarded repair on the tested controlled-fault bank; we also document an unresolved preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (the archived artifacts and transformation implementing the mapping are provided for deterministic reproduction).
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair pipelines and verifier-guided refinement have controlled empirical support in adjacent domains. Cadenas et al. (program/repair synthesis) report that verifier-interposed pipelines can increase mechanically-checkable pass rates in code-repair tasks (empirical pipeline evaluations) [1]. Recent verifier-first IaC evaluations show verifier-guided repair raises validator pass@1 on Terraform/IaC tasks under controlled settings (controlled IaC evaluation) [2]. Controlled analyses demonstrate that single-proxy verifiers may be exploited during iterative refinement, producing verifier-exploitation pathologies unless mitigations are adopted (controlled empirical caution) [3]. Empirical studies that instrument verifier-mediated agents report a measurable verifier tax—additional interaction and compute costs that affect operational tradeoffs (verifier-cost analyses) [4]. Finally, NetOps/AIOps surveys and field case studies report LLMs' usefulness for read-oriented tasks but warn about the gap between suggestions and safe closed-loop changes (surveys and field case studies) [5].

(For clarity: each bracketed citation above maps to a verified record archived with this study: [1] controlled program-repair GVR evidence; [2] verifier-first IaC evaluation; [3] controlled verifier-exploitation analysis; [4] verifier-tax instrumentation study; [5] NetOps/AIOps survey/case studies.)
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and adapter semantics. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a pair's binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and simulator-based compliance agreement (verifier+simulator). Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministic controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The declared model for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini; execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Ensuring intervention informativeness and sampling. To ensure the repair intervention could be exercised, the confirmatory sample used deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (e.g., dropped required restore, protected-interface changes). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; the execution manifest records source_generation_attempt_count = 40, source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1, and complete_pair_count = 39. Runtime sampling parameters for each model call and provider-call metadata are archived for audit: per-call provider traces and sampling records are available at execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json records the global declared settings (including temperature = null) but temperature = null does not indicate deterministic sampling.

Scoring, harmful-change mapping, and analysis plan. The primary success predicate required agreement between deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and a simulator-based compliance check. The preregistered harmful-change labeling used in the frozen transformation artifact is: label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. That transformation artifact is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode validator traces (validation_after.violation_codes) are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. The preregistered primary statistical test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial) reporting discordant counts, exact p-value, and an absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity: a single predefined primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered (primary: exclude incomplete pairs; sensitivity: treat missing episodes as failures). All per-episode artifacts and transformation manifests required to reproduce aggregated statistics are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; actual completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Supporting archived analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded per preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' because the source-generation for that task was invalid/unscorable (source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The analysis manifest documents complete_pairs = 39 and both_missing_pairs = 1; per-episode terminal errors and exclusion reasons are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic: status. The preregistration specified a confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis using the frozen harmful-change mapping; the archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because that preregistered aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim here. The compact harmful-change mapping and all per-episode traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic are archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/scoring/*.json; deterministic reproduction steps are provided in the artifact bundle and below in Reproducibility.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The confirmatory paired estimate—an absolute increase of ≈20.51 percentage points (p = 0.02148; 95% CI ≈ [7.69, 35.90] pp)—indicates that, on this preregistered synthetic controlled-fault bank and under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated success. Because each pair reused the same initial controlled-fault candidate, the contrast isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics under identical source candidates and matching repair budgets.

Mechanism and diagnostics. Archived per-episode scoring traces illustrate plausible mechanisms: guarded episodes commonly include validator_trace.violation_codes that pinpoint specific protected fields or unintended-state changes; exposing those diagnostics appears to guide the model toward targeted corrective edits (examples archived in execution/scoring/task-000002-*.json and task-000003-*.json). These per-episode traces support a concrete causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved post-repair verifier outcomes without requiring additional first-pass generations.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory test (harmful-change mapping described in Methods) was not computed by the archived confirmatory executor; therefore we explicitly treat that preregistered safety aggregation as unresolved for confirmatory claim purposes. The archived artifacts and transformation implementing the harmful-change mapping enable deterministic reproduction of the preregistered safety aggregation by independent auditors (see Reproducibility below). Any numerical harmful-overrepair counts produced outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory unless recomputed and archived following the preregistered pipeline.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The workflow required additional interaction steps: the execution manifest records hosted_model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39). These counts permit exploratory estimation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but broad operational feasibility and latency–cost tradeoffs require larger-scale studies. Practitioners should ensure verifier coverage for critical safety properties, audit harmful-change indicators (using mappings like the preregistered rules), and budget for verifier-mediated call counts.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation effects; differences across arms stem from diagnostics and repair-call behavior under the adapter contract. Construct validity: primary success depends on agreement of a deterministic verifier and a simulator; both components constrain the operational meaning of 'valid.' External validity: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank limit generalization to diverse vendor equipment and live operator streams. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed effect but limits power for detailed per-fault-class inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment under hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success on the tested synthetic task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the declared model (gpt-5-mini), the adapter semantics, and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved in this paper; the harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to compute it are archived for deterministic reproduction. We release the full artifact bundle and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json (see the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
